title: Show HN: BBRouter simulates Ben Eater's 8-bit computer on 3D virtual breadboards
content: Hi HN, I kept wiring Ben Eater's 8-bit computer wrong, so I built a realistic virtual breadboard editor. Some of the nice features are side-by-side diff, scope, schematics auto-sync, auto-router (BBRouter stands for breadboard router), and my favorites: upload from the real Arduino IDE and connect to your AI with MCP, let Claude & co build it or help you troubleshoot. The link is the SAP-1 running. You can orbit it, probe a hole with the scope, slow the clock down, play with the virtual displays for debugging, then you can actually build it following the step-by-step instructions. A side-goal is to create a community, there are quite a lot of simulators out there but mostly offline / too abstract to realistically use it for a real build. I also never found one that had a decent UI/UX and worked well on mobile or with a trackpad. Happy to answer anything, and tell me what breaks. P. S. Maker plan is $7/month; code HACKERNEWS makes the first month free and then $5/month for as long as you keep it. Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50321522 Points: 27 # Comments: 8
summary: BBRouter is a realistic virtual breadboard editor that simulates Ben Eater's 8‑bit computer with features such as side‑by‑side diff, scope, schematics auto‑sync, auto‑router, Arduino IDE upload and AI assistance. The maker plan costs $7/month; using code HACKERNEWS gives the first month free and then $5/month thereafter.

title: EU Commission confirms Polish Parliament can appoint Constitutional Court judges
content: The European Commission has stated that the Polish Parliament retains the authority to appoint judges to the Constitutional Court. This declaration follows a confrontation outside the Constitutional Tribunal building on Friday night, which was broadcast live on television and has drawn a decade‑old dispute into the broader European political debate.
summary: The EU Commission stated that the Polish Parliament has the right to appoint judges to the Constitutional Court. A confrontation outside the Constitutional Tribunal building on Friday night, broadcast live on television, has brought a decade‑old dispute into the wider European political debate.
author: Euronews

title: Rahul Gandhi leads New Delhi rally demanding election chief’s resignation
content: Thousands of demonstrators joined a protest in New Delhi on Sunday, organized by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and supported by the youth “Cockroach” movement, amid tight security. The rally called for the resignation of the country’s election chief, citing voter‑list revisions that critics claim favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s party.
summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in New Delhi on Sunday for a protest organized by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and supported by the youth Cockroach movement. Protesters are calling for the resignation of the country's election chief over voter list revisions they say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.
author: France 24

title: FBI attributes $6 billion Binance crypto theft to North Korea
content: The FBI has attributed a $6 billion theft from Binance to North Korean actors, citing “malicious cyber activity” by an entity called TraderTraitor. The same group reportedly carried out a $1.5 billion hack of the Bybit exchange last year.
summary: The FBI said North Korea was responsible for a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance. The agency linked the theft to malicious cyber activity by the group known as TraderTraitor, which also carried out a $1.5 billion Bybit hack last year.
author: DW World

title: Donald Trump loses allies after Serbia and Brazil elections
content: Following recent elections, Flavio Bolsonaro failed to gain power in Brazil and Aleksandar Vucic was voted out of office in Serbia. The same period saw a reported weakening of Benjamin Netanyahu’s position, and U.S. President Donald Trump expressed unhappiness, claiming electoral fraud.
summary: Donald Trump says the elections in Serbia and Brazil were fraudulent as he loses allies. Flavio Bolsonaro failed to gain power, Aleksandar Vucic was voted out of office, and Benjamin Netanyahu's position has weakened.
author: DW World

title: Hundreds of adult gaming centres could keep rate discounts unless bingo‑hall loophole closed
content: Hundreds of adult gaming centres in England have bingo licences that still qualify them for discounted business rates Hundreds of high street “ slot farms ” could continue claiming a discount on their business rates, unless the government closes a loophole that allows them to pose as bingo halls. John Healey singled out adult gaming centres (AGCs) in his first budget this week, in which he increased duty on slot machine takings from 20% to 25%, claiming he was “raising taxes on gambling to support good growth on every high street”.
summary: Hundreds of adult gaming centres in England hold bingo licences that qualify them for discounted business rates. In his first budget, John Healey raised duty on slot‑machine takings from 20% to 25% and warned the loophole allowing them to pose as bingo halls may need to be closed.
author: Guardian World

title: Indian security tightens Delhi perimeter before large Rahul Gandhi-led protest
content:
Indian security personnel equipped with batons, shields and riot‑control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition protest in Delhi on Sunday. The rally, which authorities said would involve traffic diversions, is set to demand the resignation of the country’s election chief over a recent revision of voter lists.  

The march will be led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi, and the opposition claims that hundreds of thousands of participants are expected, describing the event as a major challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party.
summary: Indian security tightens Delhi perimeter before large Rahul Gandhi-led protest.
author: Guardian World

title: UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister visits Denmark to study top children’s homes
content:
UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister has travelled to Copenhagen to examine the Danish residential‑care model. His visit follows concerns that England’s children’s‑home system is in crisis, prompting the British government to look abroad for possible solutions.

In a quiet suburb on the outskirts of Copenhagen, MacAlister inspected Josephine Schneider’s House, a large white building set back from the road behind a plum tree with purple leaves. The house blends in with neighboring properties and bears little outward signage, yet it is described as one of the best children’s homes in the world.

Danish children’s homes are frequently cited as the global gold standard of residential care. The British government is studying these Danish facilities as part of its effort to develop a roadmap to address the challenges facing England’s own children’s‑home system.
summary: UK children’s minister Josh MacAlister travelled to Copenhagen to examine Denmark’s residential care model, including the highly regarded Josephine Schneider’s House. The British government is studying Danish children’s homes as a possible roadmap to address the crisis in England’s own children’s home system.
author: Guardian World

title: Rachel Reeves says UK should rejoin EU, backs Andy Burnham on Brexit
content: Former chancellor says leaving European Union has made Britain ‘poorer, weaker and less secure’ The former chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK’s future should be inside the EU, saying Brexit has made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”. Writing in the Sunday Times, the Labour former cabinet minister said she welcomed “Andy Burnham’s leadership” after remarks made by the prime minister in recent days fuelled questions about the prospect of Britain returning to the bloc or adopting its freedom of movement rules.
summary: Rachel Reeves says UK should rejoin EU, backs Andy Burnham on Brexit.
author: Guardian World

title: Jacinda Ardern urges Australian politicians to rebuild trust via financial security
content: Former New Zealand prime minister has moved to Australia and is lecturing at University of Sydney – and from stage of city’s famous landmark Jacinda Ardern, who now calls Sydney home, has delivered a message to Australian politicians from the stage of the city’s Opera House. Politicians, the former New Zealand prime minister turned academic told the audience on Sunday, were exacerbating the problem of polarisation within society and needed to be better.
summary: Jacinda Ardern urges Australian politicians to rebuild trust via financial security.
author: Guardian World

title: Binance recovers 90% of $6.3bn hack losses; FBI attributes attack to North Korean group
content: Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals starting to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea. The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.
summary: Binance recovers 90% of $6.3bn hack losses; FBI attributes attack to North Korean group.
author: Guardian World

title: Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream as Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions.
summary: Newcastle’s Jaissle expressed a desire to scream during a recent event. Grealish’s performance left manager Moyes speechless.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex de Minaur defeats Alexander Zverev to reach Vienna Open final
content:
Alex de Minaur, the world No 10, defeated the world No 1‑elect Alexander Zverev 6‑4, 1‑6, 7‑6 (7‑4) in the Vienna Open semi‑final.  The Australian’s attacking style and a decisive tiebreaker—where he brushed off a couple of double faults—kept pressure on the two‑time Grand Slam champion.

The victory propels de Minaur into the championship match against Carlos Alcaraz at the Wiener Stadthalle, a win he has called one of the most significant of his career.
summary: Alex de Minaur defeated world No 1-elect Alexander Zverev 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7-4) in the Vienna Open semi‑final. The win sets up a final against Carlos Alcaraz at the Wiener Stadthalle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Atlanta Dream take early lead in Game 7 against Golden State Valkyries
content:
The 2026 WNBA Finals Game 7 is a winner‑take‑all matchup between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries, with both teams vying for their first championship. The Valkyries are hosting the Dream at their home venue.

In the first quarter, Atlanta built an 11‑2 run to take its first lead of the game. Rhyne Howard’s turnaround fadeaway gave the Dream a 11‑10 advantage with 2 minutes and 16 seconds remaining in the opening quarter.
summary: The Atlanta Dream lead 11-10 over the Golden State Valkyries after an 11‑2 run in the first quarter. Rhyne Howard scored a turnaround fadeaway to give the Dream their first lead with 2 minutes and 16 seconds remaining in the opening quarter.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Canelo Álvarez Reclaims WBC Title in Riyadh Amid Houthi Attack Concerns
content:
Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez reclaimed the WBC super‑middleweight title with a unanimous‑decision victory over the previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Saturday night. The bout was held at Kingdom Arena, with Álvarez winning by unanimous decision.

The fight proceeded amid a week of heightened security concerns in the Saudi capital. Saudi‑led coalition officials said they had intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran‑aligned Houthi forces.

Several events in the kingdom were cancelled or postponed because of the security situation, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.
summary: Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez won a unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli to regain the WBC super‑middleweight title in Riyadh. The fight proceeded at Kingdom Arena despite heightened security after the Saudi‑led coalition intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran‑aligned Houthi forces, causing cancellations of events such as the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maresca blames “silly” errors after City lose to Brighton 1-0
content: Matheus Nunes mistake lets in Yasin Ayari for winner Maresca: ‘We are conceding silly goals that we can avoid’ Enzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victory here. Ayari’s strike was made possible after Nunes, City’s right-back, missed Diego Gómez’s cross from the right, so the ball could come back across goal via Maxim De Cuyper. The 2-1 loss at Aston Villa came from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowing Nicolas Jackson’s long-range winner to squeeze under his body.
summary: Enzo Maresca said Manchester City are conceding “silly goals” after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in a 1-0 defeat. He also cited a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa where Gianluigi Donnarumma let Nicolas Jackson score a long‑range winner.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lewis Hamilton takes first Ferrari pole at Mexican Grand Prix, Antonelli fourth
content: George Russell second on grid after qualifying Antonelli well placed as he nears title confirmation Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.
summary: Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix, edging out Mercedes driver George Russell who qualified second. Kimi Antonelli qualified fourth, keeping him in contention for the title.

title: Esteban Ocon denies physical fight claim over Haas drop at Mexico City GP
content: Esteban Ocon has refuted reports suggesting his removal by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix resulted from a dispute with team principal Ayao Komatsu that escalated into a physical confrontation. Ocon says no such altercation occurred.
summary: Esteban Ocon denied reports that his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix was due to a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu. He said no physical confrontation took place.

content: Manchester United have asked about the availability of striker Ivan Toney, while Barcelona are monitoring Chelsea winger Estevao Willian. In addition, Jean‑Philippe Mateta is expected to depart Crystal Palace in January, according to the latest transfer gossip.

title: Forest coach Oliver Glasner warns he could be next sacked if wins lag
content: Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner warned that, without an improvement in results, he could become the club’s fifth sacking in just over a year. He said the pressure to secure wins is increasing and that his position depends on a swift turnaround.
summary: Oliver Glasner is the head coach of Nottingham Forest. He said he may become the club’s fifth sacking in just over a year unless results improve soon.

title: Manchester United's 9 points in 7 games suggests a full season under 30, raising relegation fears
content: Manchester United have accumulated nine points after seven league matches. At that rate, projecting the same pace over a full season would yield fewer than 30 points, a total that would typically place a club in relegation danger.
summary: Manchester United have accumulated nine points from their first seven league matches. If that scoring rate continued, they would finish the season with fewer than 30 points.

title: North Korean hacking group linked to $6.3B Binance breach
content: A North Korea‑based cybercrime group is identified as the source of a $6.3 billion hack of the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the incident—the largest crypto hack on record—to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit previously known for targeting the digital‑asset sector.
summary: A North Korea-based cybercrime group is alleged to have hacked Binance for $6.3 billion. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis tied the breach to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit that has previously targeted the digital asset industry.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ film critiques modern manufactured reality
content: The film “You Can See Everything,” created by Fielder and Oppenheim, presents a view in which everything can be seen, yet the creators emphasize that seeing does not equal knowing. According to the description, the film’s effectiveness stems from its awareness of this distinction.
summary: The film “You Can See Everything” shows that seeing everything does not equal knowing. Directors Fielder and Oppenheim make the film effective by recognizing this distinction.

title: Blackburn's governor bid opens possible Senate seat for Defense Secretary Hegseth
content: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R‑Tenn.) is running for Tennessee’s governorship, creating a vacancy in the state’s Senate delegation. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a former Army National Guard major, has expressed interest in the open Senate seat and is regarded as a likely oversight target in the next Congress should House Democrats win the majority.
summary: Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s (R-Tenn.) bid to become Tennessee’s next governor is leaving a potential opening for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who is viewed as one of the top oversight targets in the next Congress if House Democrats take the majority.

title: New autism study complicates Trump administration’s search for cause
content: A newly published study identified links between specific maternal health conditions during pregnancy and autism diagnoses across racial and ethnic groups. The research, conducted by investigators at the New York University Grossman School of Medicine and the Kaiser Permanent School of Medicine, highlights the limited understanding that persists as the Trump administration seeks a cause of autism.
summary: New autism study complicates Trump administration’s search for cause.

title: El‑Sayed accuses Stevens of relitigating primary after she urges apology on Israel
content:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed (D) rebuked former primary rival Rep. Haley Stevens (D‑Mich.) after she said he should apologize for comments he made about Israel, a demand made only days before the upcoming Senate contest.  

Stevens responded that she would appear alongside El‑Sayed for the first time since their August primary.
summary: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) is firing back on his former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.), after she expected him to apologize over his comments on Israel just a few days out from the high-stakes Michigan Senate race.

content: Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom released a “Sinners”-themed campaign advertisement on TikTok over Halloween weekend, just days before the midterm elections. The spot references an Academy Award‑winning film set in the 1932 Mississippi Delta starring Michael B. Jordan as twins, using the movie’s premise as a backdrop for the ad.
summary: Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom released a “Sinners”-themed campaign ad over Halloween weekend, days before the midterm elections. The TikTok ad references the Academy Award‑winning film set in the Mississippi Delta in 1932 starring Michael B. Jordan as twins.

content: An advisor to Rep. Jim Clyburn said Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed cannot rescind the invitation extended to his former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, for a Sunday event in Detroit. Antjuan Seawright told The New York Times the invitation “still stands” because the gathering is not El‑Sayed’s event.

content: Virginia and the District of Columbia have filed a lawsuit seeking to halt the construction of a Trump‑named arch. U.S. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkin directed the parties to confer and agree on a proposed briefing schedule for the motion seeking a temporary restraining order, with the schedule due by Saturday evening.
summary: Virginia and D.C. file lawsuit to halt Trump arch construction.
author: NPR Politics

title: Reflective lava world found among Kepler and TESS ultra‑short‑period planets
content: Kepler and TESS have identified a class of ultra‑short‑period (USP) exoplanets that complete an orbit in less than 24 hours. These worlds move far more quickly around their stars than Mercury, which ancient astronomers named for the swift Roman messenger after observing its 88‑day orbit. The comparison highlights just how rapid the orbital periods of the newly discovered USPs are relative to the innermost planet of our own solar system.
summary: Kepler and TESS have discovered ultra‑short‑period (USP) exoplanets that orbit their stars in under 24 hours. Ancient astronomers named Mercury for its speed, but Mercury is far slower than these USPs.
author: Phys.org

title: Filmmaker Zarina Zabrisky gives France 24 interview on recent Oleshky events
content: American filmmaker Zarina Zabrisky, who has lived and reported across the Dnipro River in Ukrainian‑controlled Kherson for three years, is providing testimonies to France 24’s Gavin Lee about events that occurred in the past 24 hours. The interview focuses on recent developments in the Oleshky area.
summary: American filmmaker Zarina Zabrisky, who has lived and reported across the Dnipro River in Ukrainian‑controlled Kherson for three years, is speaking to France 24’s Gavin Lee. She discusses events that occurred in Oleshky during the past 24 hours.

title: Poland PM Donald Tusk defends constitutional court overhaul despite protests
content:
Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, said the overhaul of the country’s constitutional court is essential to restore a tribunal he described as “crippled by years of political disputes.” In a prime‑time television address on Saturday night, Tusk declared that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise” and vowed to push the contested reform forward.

He made the remarks while riot police were deployed overnight to protect the court’s building amid protests against the plan.
summary: Poland’s prime minister Donald Tusk said the constitutional court overhaul is vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes. He defended the plan in a Saturday night television address, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building.
author: Guardian World

title: Kane misses penalty as Bayern Munich draws 2-2 with Dortmund
content:
Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 in Der Klassiker on Saturday, a result that left the two teams level on points at the top of the league. The match featured a late equalizer from Borussia Dortmund’s Fabio Silva, who scored in the final moments to secure the share of spoils for his side.

Harry Kane, the recent Ballon d’Or winner, started the match for Bayern Munich but missed a penalty kick while his team led 1-0. Kane had been an unused substitute during Bayern’s 6-1 German Cup victory over Magdeburg on Wednesday but returned to the starting lineup for the league fixture.

In addition to the missed penalty, Kane struck the post during the encounter. The incident was one of four times Bayern Munich hit the woodwork in the game.
summary: Harry Kane missed a penalty and hit the post as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker. A last-gasp equaliser by Fabio Silva kept the teams level on points at the top of the league.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Naderi’s late goal secures Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup final spot
content:
Ryan Naderi scored a dramatic late goal to lead Rangers to a 1-0 victory over Aberdeen at Hampden Park, securing their spot in the Premier Sports Cup final. After a low-quality first half where Rangers managed only one shot on target, Aberdeen’s manager Derek McInnes’s side increased their pace in the second half.

Despite surviving sustained pressure from the visitors, Aberdeen conceded in the 83rd minute when Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net. The goal marked Naderi’s eighth of the season, breaking down the home side’s stubborn resistance to seal the win.
summary: Ryan Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice in the 83rd minute to score Rangers’ only goal in a 1-0 win over Aberdeen at Hampden Park. The victory secures Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jonathan Wilson: Mikel Arteta's "dossier" strategy is dangerous for Arsenal
content: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”
summary: Mikel Arteta collected images of rival managers leaving their technical areas after receiving his second booking for doing so. Jonathan Wilson argues that this approach, which Arteta defends as a counter to perceived bias, is a dangerous tactic for the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex Mitchell limps off with hamstring as Northampton beat Gloucester 28-14
content:
Northampton secured a 28-14 victory over Gloucester, a result that underscores the team’s defensive resilience against early-season pace-setters. The match highlighted the absence of England scrum-half Alex Mitchell, who limped off with a suspected hamstring pull, adding to the national team’s injury concerns ahead of next Sunday’s autumn opener against Australia. Despite the setback, Northampton weathered the loss to score 28 unanswered points after withstanding Gloucester’s early onslaught.

The performance marked a stark contrast to Northampton’s previous league outing, where 119 points were scored. This victory was built on strong defensive efforts, with Tom Pearson, who is back in the England picture this autumn, delivering an outstanding display throughout the game.
summary: Alex Mitchell left the match with a suspected hamstring pull, making his participation in England’s upcoming autumn opener against Australia uncertain. Despite his exit, Northampton held off Gloucester to win 28‑14, scoring 28 unanswered points.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick to lead Manchester United against Roma after Chelsea defeat
content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has confirmed he will remain in charge for the upcoming Champions League match against Roma on Tuesday. This assurance comes despite the team’s 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday, which extended United’s winless streak to nine games. Carrick is currently navigating a difficult period, as the club has endured its longest such run since 1988.

During his post-match analysis, Carrick focused on defensive errors, specifically highlighting the moment Morgan Rogers scored for Chelsea. Rogers broke through the center of United’s defense, a goal Carrick described as a significant turning point when the match was balanced. While acknowledging the severity of conceding in that manner, Carrick stated he is now concentrating on preparing his players for the midweek fixture.
summary: Michael Carrick stated he will remain in charge for Manchester United's upcoming Champions League match against Roma. The manager made this declaration after a 2-0 loss to Chelsea extended the club's winless run to nine games.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Canelo Álvarez v Christian Mbilli: WBC super-middleweight championship – live
content:
Canelo Álvarez is set to challenge Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight championship at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh. The Mexican star enters the bout as the underdog, fighting for the first time since his loss to Crawford. Mbilli, the defending champion, made his entrance first, wearing a black tee and red trunks. He was followed by Álvarez, who arrived after an extended video introduction, accompanied by his team and recording artist Tito Double P.

The fighters’ ringwalks were notably subdued, lacking the pyrotechnics typically associated with Álvarez. The pre-fight ceremony at the Kingdom Arena included the performance of three national anthems. First, the national anthem of Saudi Arabia was played to honor the hosts. This was followed by La Marseillaise for Mbilli and the Himno Nacional Mexicano for Álvarez. The article notes that the fighters were expected to begin their entrances at the time of the live report.
summary: Álvarez challenges for Mbilli’s 168lb title in Riyadh Mexican star fights for first time since Crawford loss Reach out to Bryan on Bluesky or by email Here come the fighters. First it’s Mbilli, entering first despite his status as the champion, wearing a black tee and red trunks.

title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham equaliser
content:
Fulham’s victory reinforced Jamie Carragher’s claim that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.  The hosts demonstrated they can grind out a point on a bad day and will head to Barcelona on Tuesday with confidence.

Zion Suzuki’s own goal denied Unai Emery’s Villa a fifth win in six games.  Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had earlier promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the Premier League’s top third.
summary: Fulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence.

content:
Lewis Hamilton secured pole position in the Mexican Grand Prix qualifying session.

content: Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made a second‑half mistake that allowed Fulham to secure a 1‑1 draw at Villa Park. Nicolas Jackson had earlier given the hosts the lead, but the error by Suzuki tipped the match into a stalemate.
summary: Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made a second‑half mistake that allowed Fulham to secure a 1‑1 draw at Villa Park. The hosts had taken the lead earlier when Nicolas Jackson scored.

title: Six Senate Seats Could Decide Midterm Control
content:
The upcoming midterm election will determine Senate control through a handful of highly competitive contests. Six seats—Texas, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas—are rated as “toss‑ups” by DDHQ and are currently held by Republicans.

These six races represent the only paths for either party to secure an upper‑chamber majority. The GOP’s best chance of flipping a seat remains to be seen.
summary: The midterm tug-of-war for Senate control will come down to six toss‑up seats held by Republicans in Texas, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas. Both parties see a path to majority in the upper chamber based on these contests.

title: Olivia Rodrigo gives flowers to Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton at Columbus concert

content: Researchers have identified a gene encoding a tandem potassium channel in an algal virus. The study appears in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

title: Nighttime bat surveys aid science and reshape public perception
content:
People often react with curiosity when they hear a chirping sound on a detector or feel something whiz past, moments that signal an encounter with microbats. The title notes that seeking these animals after dark can aid scientific research and shift public perception of the creatures.

Microbats are described as small, primarily nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. They emit calls and listen to the returning echoes to locate objects and prey.
summary: Researchers conduct after‑dark searches for microbats, which are small nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. The resulting data can advance scientific knowledge and change how people view these animals.

title: NES Contra 1987 ported from assembly to C and WebAssembly with online co‑op
content:
A Show HN post announces a browser‑based port of the 1987 NES game Contra. The author used vermiceli’s annotated disassembly of the original ROM as a reference, translating the 6502 assembly routine by routine into C and verifying each frame against the original using the Mesen emulator. The resulting C code was then compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the game to run in a web browser.

The port adds online multiplayer, enabling two players to cooperate over the internet. The project’s source code is hosted on GitHub, and the submission has received 28 points and 17 comments on Hacker News.
summary: The 1987 NES game Contra was translated routine‑by‑routine from its 6502 assembly into C and then compiled to WebAssembly to run in a browser. The port adds online multiplayer so two players can play co‑op over the internet.

title: Pakistan clinch tri-series final as Fakhar Zaman scores 127 to beat Sri Lanka
content:
Pakistan clinched the tri‑series title in a dramatic final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium. The packed-out venue saw the match settled in the penultimate over, with Pakistan defeating Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the tournament under the lights.

In the chase of 326, Fakhar Zaman delivered the headline performance, smashing 127 off 99 balls. After his dismissal the new batsmen had to remain composed, and the partnership that followed proved decisive.

Arafat Minhas (21) and Hasan Nawaz (24) forged a 94‑run stand that secured the win. Minhas and Faheem Ashraf were dismissed with two runs still required, but Shaheen Afridi finished the evening with a powerful boundary over the ropes. Sri Lankan opener Kamindu Mendis also scored 131, but his efforts could not prevent Pakistan’s victory.
summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, chasing 326. Fakhar Zaman made 127 off 99 balls, supported by a 94‑run partnership from Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz, and Shaheen Afridi hit the winning runs.

title: Glasner defiant as Brentford exploit Nottingham Forest woes
content: For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest, the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”. “For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation than the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.”
summary: Oliver Glasner held a 14-minute press conference where he blamed himself for compromising principles and told Nottingham Forest players to leave if they did not buy in. He stated that the club must change and rebuild from the bottom to the top without any compromises.

title: UChicago researchers find radiation-activated TET2 locks immune cells in suppressive state
content:

TET2 removes chemical tags from RNA, locking these cells into an immune‑suppressing state. By targeting this pathway, the researchers suggest the possibility of reprogramming the cells so they attack tumors instead of protecting them.
summary: Researchers at the University of Chicago identified a mechanism by which radiation therapy reprograms immune cells to protect tumors rather than attack them. title: Boot Sector Language Model Generates Infinite Linux Boot Logs
content:
A new language model project has been showcased on Hacker News, featuring an inference engine that fits entirely within a 510-byte Master Boot Record (MBR). The project draws inspiration from the boot sector demo scene, where developers previously created applications such as chess games and C compilers in 512 bytes. This neural network generates Linux boot logs for non-existent hardware by producing dmesg messages infinitely. The system utilizes a small character-level network trained on dmesg data, with the weights, vocabulary, and strings stored in the sectors immediately following the MBR.

During development, the creator identified a specific bug by comparing the output of a Python simulator with the assembly code running in QEMU. Although the initial characters matched, the output eventually diverged. By retrieving hidden layer values via QEMU’s debug port, it was determined that only the first neuron was calculated correctly. The issue stemmed from the idiv instruction, which stores its remainder in the edx register, overwriting the pointer to the biases table. This caused the first neuron to be biased correctly while subsequent neurons used garbage data. The fix involved determining the bias address from the loop counter to ensure no pointers survived the division operation.

A second bug was discovered by inspecting the code before the initial run. The BIOS print routine zeros out the bx register, which contained the predicted character number. This necessitated the use of push and pop instructions to preserve the value of bx around the print call. The project contrasts with Sectorllm, which runs a 5-layer Llama2 model with an attention mechanism in 1.2K of assembly code. In contrast, this project prioritizes fitting the engine into a single sector, resulting in a network with just one hidden layer of int8 operations.
summary: A 510‑byte MBR contains an inference engine that uses a small char‑level neural network to generate Linux boot messages infinitely. The author debugged integer‑arithmetic bugs, fixing bias pointer and BIOS print routine issues to match QEMU output.

title: Binance CEO says 90% of $6.3B stolen assets have been replenished
content:
Binance disclosed that hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from its customers in what it described as a record‑breaking crypto heist. The company’s chief executive said the firm has already replenished about 90 percent of the stolen assets and intends to cover the remaining 10 percent, which consists of “less liquid” tokens that may take longer to acquire.

Binance added that withdrawals remain paused but are expected to resume on Sunday, reiterating its commitment to fully absorb the financial impact of the incident.
summary: Binance CEO said the firm has replaced 90 percent of the $6.3 billion taken from customers and will cover the remaining 10 percent, which consists of less‑liquid tokens that may take longer to acquire. Withdrawals remain paused but are expected to be reenabled on Sunday.
author: The Verge

title: France limits two anti‑racism rallies near Paris to eastern outskirts
content:
Two rallies against racism are scheduled to take place near Paris, according to the report’s headline. The events are set against a broader wave of unrest, as France prepares for a third weekend of protests over the rising cost of living. Authorities anticipate nearly half a million participants nationwide and have mobilized 70,000 police officers to maintain order.

In Paris, a last‑minute court ruling has limited today’s march to the city’s eastern outskirts. The coverage of these developments is provided by Jack Pownall.
summary: France is preparing for a third weekend of protests over the rising cost of living, with nearly half a million people expected nationwide and 70,000 police deployed. A last‑minute court ruling restricted the two anti‑racism rallies near Paris to the city’s eastern outskirts.
author: France 24

title: French Interior Minister fears disorder after dark on Halloween
content:
Saturday will see another day of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and school conditions, described as “Act Three” and uniting Yellow Vest activists with student demonstrators. France’s highest administrative court has upheld a ban on the planned Paris march route, requiring protesters to stay on the city’s eastern outskirts.

Authorities are deploying 70,000 security personnel and imposing curfews in some areas, echoing measures used last weekend. The interior minister issued a Halloween‑themed warning that covering one’s face at a demonstration remains illegal, according to Ophelie Jacobson.
summary: Saturday is set to see another day of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and conditions in schools. Dubbed “Act Three”, the protests bring together Yellow Vest activists and student demonstrators.
author: France 24

title: European ministers confront Russia's Lavrov and skip group photo at G20
content:
The G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the United States is concluding two days of talks without reaching agreement on several key global security issues. On the sidelines, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an Arctic cooperation agreement with Japan and South Korea and confirmed Washington’s participation in Riyadh’s World Expo in 2030.

European ministers confronted Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov over the war in Ukraine and declined to join him for the traditional group photo, highlighting the division caused by Russia’s presence at the summit. Jack Pownall reports.
summary: The G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the US is wrapping up two days of talks without agreement on several key global security issues. On the sidelines, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an Arctic cooperation deal with Japan and South Korea and confirmed Washington’s participation in Riyadh’s World Expo in 2030.
author: France 24

title: Dozens protest at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, several detained
content: Police in Poland increased security around the Constitutional Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered on Friday to oppose the government’s suspension of its president, a move the demonstrators claim is unlawful. Several people were detained after some protesters breached the court’s perimeter fence, according to police. Charlotte Hughes reports.
summary: Police increased security around the Constitutional Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered on Friday to oppose the government's suspension of its president, which they called unlawful. Police said several people were detained after some demonstrators breached the court's perimeter fence.
author: France 24

title: UK PM Andy Burnham open to slavery apology, rejects financial reparations
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing its first apology for its role in the trans‑Atlantic slave trade, but he rejected calls for financial reparations. The debate comes as King Charles continues his visit to three Caribbean nations ahead of the Commonwealth summit.
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Saturday he was “open” to the UK apologising for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but rejected calls for financial reparations. The issue has featured prominently during King Charles’s ongoing visit to three Caribbean nations ahead of a Commonwealth summit.
author: France 24

title: Oleshky Residents Reunite with Families After Rescue Operation
content: On Saturday, evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory during a major rescue operation. They had traveled through Belarus amid a rare truce brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022, and intense fighting left residents starving and unable to leave.
summary: Evacuees from Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory Saturday in a major rescue operation after traveling through Belarus during a rare truce brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. The city has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and was caught in intense fighting that left residents starving and unable to leave.
author: France 24

title: Khamenei warns US and Israel against new attacks amid Middle East tensions
content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a warning on Saturday, telling the United States and Israel not to carry out additional strikes as concerns grow about renewed fighting in the Middle East. The warning follows recent threats of military action against Iran made by U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not yet decided on any new strikes.
summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against further strikes. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump had not yet decided on fresh attacks.
author: France 24

title: Government corruption tops concerns of US midterm voters, poll shows
content:
A recent exclusive poll indicates that government corruption has emerged as a top issue for voters heading into the US midterm elections. The article highlights that alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies is becoming a significant concern for the electorate. This shift in voter sentiment contrasts with historical political narratives, such as the “welfare queen” trope popularized by Ronald Reagan in 1976, which focused on fraud by the poor rather than high-level governmental misconduct.

The text details several specific allegations of financial entanglements involving the Trump administration and its associates. It notes that the Qatari government gifted the president a luxury jet, a move that potentially violates the emoluments clause of the constitution. Additionally, the UAE reportedly gained access to high-end American AI chips shortly after an investment firm linked to its ruling family purchased a $500 million stake in World Liberty Financial, a crypto company funded by the families of Trump and Steve Witkoff.

Further examples of alleged self-dealing include the pardons granted to Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and Julio Herrera Velutini, a banker who paid her bribes. These pardons followed a $50 million deal between Velutini’s family and Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, as well as a $3.5 million donation to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The article also points to the Pentagon lending over $600 million to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, acquired a stake in the company.

Finally, the piece mentions Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Trump, which is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies. The source characterizes this as enriching the president’s children from a war launched without consulting Congress. These incidents collectively form the basis for the growing voter concern regarding corruption in the government.
summary: An exclusive poll found that government corruption is a top issue for US midterm voters. The report cites alleged self‑dealing by President Trump and his allies, including a Qatari‑gifted luxury jet, UAE access to American AI chips after a stake purchase, and donations linked to pardons.
author: Guardian World

title: Judge rules firing of assistant US attorney Maurene Comey unlawful
content:
Legal experts praised a recent decision that blocked the dismissal of Maurene Comey, an assistant U.S. attorney, while cautioning that an appeal is probable. Judge Jesse Furman ruled this week that the Justice Department’s termination of Comey “without cause” was unlawful, a judgment that veterans said could send a strong message about politicized firings and affect other judges handling similar cases.

Maurene Comey, the daughter of former FBI director James Comey, previously handled high‑profile prosecutions in the Southern District of New York, securing guilty verdicts against Ghislaine Maxwell and Sean “Diddy” Combs. The ruling is being viewed as a potential check on efforts perceived as attacks on the rule of law.
summary: Judge Jesse Furman this week ruled that the Department of Justice’s firing of assistant US attorney Maurene Comey without cause was unlawful. Legal experts said the decision could send a strong message about politicized firings and may be appealed.
author: Guardian World

title: Over 50.5 million early votes cast with three days left before US midterms
content:
More than 50.5 million Americans have cast early ballots as of Saturday morning, three days before the U.S. midterm elections, according to an analysis by the University of Florida. The tally represents a record number of early votes and is nearly five million higher than the total early votes recorded in the 2022 midterms.

The surge in early voting is occurring amid a series of tight contests that will determine control of Congress. In the states that collect party‑affiliation data, Democrats have outnumbered Republicans among early voters.
summary: More than 50.5 million early votes have been cast across the United States as of Saturday morning, according to a University of Florida analysis. That total is nearly 5 million higher than the early voting total in the 2022 midterm election and Democrats outnumber Republicans in states that report party data.
author: Guardian World

title: Virginia and DC file federal lawsuit to block Trump memorial arch as construction looms
content:
Legal challenges to Donald Trump’s proposed memorial arch are mounting, with the District of Columbia and Virginia filing a federal lawsuit on Saturday. The administration says construction could begin as early as next week.  

There are now three lawsuits seeking to halt work on a monument that would rise 250 ft (76 m) on a grass patch off the bridge spanning the Potomac River, which connects the city with Arlington National Cemetery. The arch would be 100 ft (30 m) taller than the Statue of Liberty from its base to the torch.
summary: The District of Columbia and Virginia filed a federal lawsuit on Saturday seeking to stop Donald Trump’s proposed 250‑foot memorial arch. The administration says construction could begin as early as next week, and the arch would be 100 feet taller than the Statue of Liberty from its base to the torch.
author: Guardian World

title: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests
content:
Clashes erupted in Paris, Marseille, and other French cities following a third wave of protests concerning the cost of living and deteriorating public services. According to the interior ministry, approximately 320,000 people participated in rallies nationwide, a decrease from the estimated 410,000 attendees the previous weekend. In Paris, 70,000 demonstrators, some wearing Halloween costumes, marched along boulevards on the south-eastern outskirts, deliberately avoiding the city centre.

Simultaneous demonstrations occurred in Germany, where police deployed teargas to disperse crowds as evening approached. The French protests marked the third consecutive weekend of unrest, with masked rioters engaging in clashes with police forces in several major cities.
summary: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests.
author: Guardian World

title: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families after truce permits crossing into Ukraine
content:
Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The crossing occurred under a truce described as the most significant since Russia’s full‑scale invasion began four and a half years ago, and the major rescue operation that enabled it started on Friday.

Residents of nearby villages lined the highway, waving flags to greet the convoy as it entered the area. The operation facilitated the movement of the Oleshky evacuees across the front line during the brief cease‑fire.
summary: Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The major rescue operation began on Friday and was carried out under the most significant truce since Russia’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago.
author: Guardian World

title: Artists in Albanese's Grayndler seat rally against AI content-scraping proposal
content: Inner west Sydney seat has long been safely held by the PM – but potential changes to copyright laws are angering its large creative community Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The prime minister is facing growing discontent within his own electorate as creatives push back against the federal government’s proposal to allow AI companies to scrape everything Australians create online. Anthony Albanese’s seat of Grayndler in Sydney’s inner west is home to more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses, and 10% of its workers are employed in cultural and creative fields – compared with 4.2% nationally.
summary: Creative workers in the Grayndler electorate are pushing back against the federal government's proposal to allow AI companies to scrape everything Australians create online. The seat, held by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, includes more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses and has 10% of its workers employed in cultural and creative fields.
author: Guardian World
